summary: Gone L-5 cab lookout on McCoy Peak in the Gifford Pinchot forest; the sources disagree on whether it was removed or burned in 1964.

facts.status_note: The register says the cab was removed in 1964. FireLookout.com says destroyed in 1964, and WillhiteWeb quotes a 1964 survey record of destruction by fire on September 10, 1964

visit.trail_note: Original trail from the north along Langille Ridge; WillhiteWeb says roads wash out often and advises checking Forest Service road status

events.note: Built shortly after the July 1934 photographs; standing by 1937 at the latest. The register gives only 'the 1930s'
Occupied for several years after the 1940 Langille Ridge fire; exact years not given
A 1964 survey crew recorded the lookout as destroyed by fire on September 10, 1964
Register says the L-5 cab was removed in 1964; conflicts with the destroyed entries
Registered on the Former Fire Lookout Sites register July 16, 2012

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register says the cab was removed in 1964. FireLookout.com and the WillhiteWeb survey record say it was destroyed in 1964, the record by fire on September 10. The story reports both and does not pick one.
The register panorama caption is dated 7-16-1934, while WillhiteWeb says the site was photographed July 18, 1934. The story uses WillhiteWeb's date for its own statement.

notes_for_editor: Two registers agree the 1930s build but disagree on the 1964 end (removed vs destroyed). Most of the detail rests on one personal website; no Forest Service record was found. Kresek's book was not reached. No staffing end date or fire cause is given. Access is not recorded because no source states a closure or permit rule.
